To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new approach, involving the micro-dissection of tissue sections, was developed to identify and quantify proteins from a specific area of a tissue section, leading to the generation of images based on relative protein quantification.
a novel parafilm assisted tissue microdissection strategy was developed to identify and quantify proteins in a specific region of a tissue section.
we developed a new technique, PAM, to perform microdissection and protein extraction from a defined region on a tissue mounted on parafilmed glass slide.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of a new strategy for the identification of large numbers of proteins from a tissue sample, based on MALDI MS imaging and the use of the PAM technique.
the development of a new method for the identification of a large number of proteins from tissue sections by microdissection.
the development of a new method of microdissection of biological tissues mounted on a paraffin film-covered slide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PAM is an interesting strategy that can be used to identify proteins and quantify them in a given tissue area.
PAM is a powerful method that can be used to generate images of a tissue based on the quantification of proteins.
PAM-MSI allows the mapping of the spatial localization of proteins and the identification of their abundance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PAM method is a powerful strategy for the identification and relative quantification of proteins in tissue samples, allowing a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms involved in a given pathology or phenotype.

parafilm assisted mass spectrometry (PAM) imaging is a new strategy to highlight regions with specific phenotypes based molecular content and to quantify the relative amount of proteins in these regions.
we have developed an efficient method to identify proteins by MALDI MSI and to quantify them in the different areas of the tissue section.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the parafilm-assistance allows to obtain high-quality data in the MS analysis, and that the parafilmed glass slide allows to perform the excision of a specific area of the tissue section, thus providing a new strategy for MALDI-MSI-based protein quantification.
parafilm can be used for the collection and storage of tissue extracts for subsequent protein identification and quantification by LC-MS/MS.
PAM can be used for the identification and quantification of proteins and that the combination of MALDI MSI and PAM can be applied to the analysis of complex tissues.
